claims.text: The target alloy has an approximate composition of 30 at% Ti, 30 at% Ni, 20 at% Cr, 10 at% Al, and 10 at% Y.
The intervention incorporates 1 vol% nano-Y2O3 through mechanical alloying followed by consolidation at 1000°C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere.
The prescribed intervention will produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y2O3 particles in the alloy matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain stable during elevated-temperature exposure.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as barriers to dislocation movement.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will stabilize or pin grain boundaries.
Blocking dislocation movement will impede plastic deformation.
Grain-boundary stabilization will impede grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
The Y2O3-treated alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the untreated alloy.
The Y2O3-treated alloy will have improved elevated-temperature creep resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement will depend on nanoparticle dispersion quality and thermal stability.
An inert atmosphere will minimize oxidation during processing.
The selected consolidation temperature and duration balance densification against retention of a uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
Maintaining 1 vol% Y2O3, a 1000°C consolidation temperature, and an inert atmosphere will avoid oxide agglomeration or unwanted phase formation.
TEM/SEM with EDS mapping can determine whether the oxide particles are homogeneously distributed.
